sources.title: Handling Update Conflicts — PowerSync
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling official docs; no release pin at URL. Captured 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Handling Update Conflicts; upload queue and operations; lines 127-151
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Backend is application-defined; client mutations are ordered, must be sequentially drained and may repeat. Simplest handler is per-field LWW with delete-wins; custom logic may validate/reject. CRDTs can be stored as data but are not built-in operation semantics.
sources.applicability: Primary candidate for offline queue and backend-owned policy; transport behavior is not roster validation, authorization, approval, or publication.

sources.title: Custom Conflict Resolution — PowerSync
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling official docs; no release pin at URL. Captured 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Sequence-number versioning §2 lines 389-391; field-level LWW §3 lines 451-453; server-side conflict recording §5 lines 661-699; change-level status tracking §6 lines 853-875
sources.observed_operation: Read official documentation examples and conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Clock-based checks can give false conflicts under clock skew; docs recommend server-managed sequence numbers for critical data. Whole-row version compare rejects all when stale; field-level LWW only allows independent fields and requires per-field metadata. Conflict records can preserve both sides for user action.
sources.applicability: Patterns to adapt for field edits, stale constrained commands, and visible rejected changes. Snippets are illustrative and were not executed or treated as production-safe.

sources.title: Sync Streams Are Now Generally Available — PowerSync
sources.released_version_or_commit: Official announcement; GA status; service v1.20.0+ and latest SDK versions with Rust sync client listed as requirements.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Edition 3 config required; Sync Streams filters data per authenticated user using auth.user_id(); legacy Sync Rules continue working. Authentication/filtering controls downloaded rows, not backend write authorization.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 constraints
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 documentation; current supported version shown at capture; 19 listed as development.
sources.locator: 5.5 constraints, especially CHECK warning lines 92-101 and exclusion constraints lines 377-388; foreign keys lines 242-284
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CHECK constraints cannot safely reference other rows/tables. Use supported UNIQUE/EXCLUDE/FK constraints for cross-row restrictions; exclusion constraints use specified operators and create an index. Exact range/operator/index setup must be validated for chosen schema/extensions.
sources.applicability: Conditional server-side enforcement for no-overlap and relationships if PostgreSQL is selected; not a complete qualification/dependency rule engine.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 Row Security Policies
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 documentation; current supported version at access.
sources.locator: §5.9 lines 20-30 and examples; referential-integrity caveat lines 182-185
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: RLS is disabled by default; when enabled with no policy it defaults to deny; table owners normally bypass it and superuser/BYPASSRLS always bypass. Referential-integrity checks bypass RLS.
sources.applicability: Server read/write isolation aid only when enabled and role-tested; cannot by itself express the supervisor's approval workflow.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 SET TRANSACTION
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 documentation; current supported version at access.
sources.locator: Isolation-level section lines 38-53; default note lines 81-86
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Default isolation is READ COMMITTED. SERIALIZABLE detects nonserializable concurrent patterns by aborting a transaction with serialization_failure; callers must retry. Level must be selected before first query/write.
sources.applicability: Candidate for transactionally checking multi-row roster invariants; application must implement rollback/retry and conflict feedback.

sources.title: SQLite transaction control
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Multiple readers but one simultaneous writer; default transaction mode is DEFERRED; upgrade to writer can fail SQLITE_BUSY; IMMEDIATE obtains writer reservation up front but can also be busy.
sources.applicability: Local atomic edit/persistence behavior and adapter test requirements; local transaction does not validate a disconnected global schedule.

sources.title: SQLite Foreign Key Support
sources.released_version_or_commit: SQLite docs; FK support introduced in 3.6.19; current compile/runtime behavior must be checked.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Foreign-key enforcement is disabled by default and must be enabled/checkable separately on every connection; cannot be toggled inside an active transaction.
sources.applicability: Local reference checks only if the chosen SQLite client/connection enables FK enforcement; does not enforce center-wide overlap across unsynced clients.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.locator: Advantages/disadvantages lines 66-81; checkpointing and concurrency lines 87-99
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL allows concurrent readers and a writer, but only one writer; requires same-host shared memory and does not work on a network filesystem; automatic checkpoint threshold defaults to 1000 pages.
sources.applicability: Local storage mode/recovery and portability requirements, conditional on target platform.

sources.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.locator: flush/fsync and OS dependency lines 137-145; crash-testing lines 405-416; failure limitations lines 421-434
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: SQLite flushes at critical points and has extensive simulated crash tests, but relies on correct OS/filesystem/device flush and locking; some broken flush implementations can still permit corruption.
sources.applicability: Supports a local recovery test plan with platform caveat; does not promise recovery of an unsynced device lost/corrupt database.

sources.title: SQLite PRAGMA integrity_check
sources.locator: PRAGMA integrity_check lines 496-513; journal-mode default lines 515-526
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: integrity_check checks structural consistency and unique/check/not-null constraints but not foreign-key errors; use foreign_key_check separately. quick_check is faster but omits unique/index consistency checks.
sources.applicability: Recovery diagnostics/proposed QA only; a check is not a backup strategy.

sources.title: Automerge getConflicts API v3.5.0
sources.locator: getConflicts description lines 5-12 and same-key conflict example lines 25-45
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Concurrent puts to the same map key produce competing values; one is surfaced deterministically/arbitrarily, while getConflicts can inspect the alternatives.
sources.applicability: Candidate for collaborative note/document content; convergence is not schedule validity or approval.

sources.title: CouchDB replication and conflict model
sources.released_version_or_commit: Apache CouchDB 3.5 documentation branch; release notes list 3.5.x patches; exact deployment patch not selected.
sources.locator: §2.3 replication, deterministic winner, conflict reads, revision tree, view behavior
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Concurrent document leaves replicate non-destructively, but deterministic winner is default view/read state; other leaves require conflicts=true/open_revs and application merge. Same-node stale _rev update returns 409. winning_revs_only replication discards conflicts.
sources.applicability: Alternative for offline document replication when application explicitly handles conflicts; relational multi-row roster rules need additional policy code.

sources.title: CouchDB document design considerations
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Single-document aggregation may leave unsatisfactory whole-document conflicts; splitting fields into documents changes the unit of conflict and raises ordering/duplicate/history considerations. Revision history is not intended as application version history.
sources.applicability: Representation tradeoff for CouchDB alternative; published roster versions should still be explicit application data.
